deck.title: Why Harbor Bikes riders leave
deck.subtitle: Fictional demo deck, not real data
deck.intro: A fictional demo built by FilmDeck from a storyboard. Every figure shown comes from the demo brief. Sound is on, best viewed fullscreen.
deck.audience: Demo audience for the FilmDeck generator

sources.label: Fictional demo brief about the made-up company Harbor Bikes. Not real data.

scenes.idea: Open on the quiet loss of riders nobody asks about.
scenes.visualDirection: Letterbox, slow serif lines, one giant word.

beats.notes: Start slowly. Riders do not announce that they are leaving, they just stop renewing.
The real problem is that nobody has ever asked them why.
Today we look at why riders leave Harbor Bikes. This is a fictional demo company.

scenes.title: Churn has nearly doubled.
scenes.idea: Monthly churn went up from a lower level to a higher one.
scenes.visualDirection: Large central gauge, needle sweeps then jumps to the alarm band.

beats.notes: Here is the problem. We measure monthly churn, the share of riders who leave.
It used to sit here, at the level shown on the gauge.

beats.summary: Needle jumps to the current rate.
beats.notes: Now it has jumped to the level you see. That is almost double.

scenes.title: Why do riders switch?
scenes.idea: Rival price cuts are far bigger than our loyalty discount.
scenes.visualDirection: Two range bars on one scale, a bracket for the gap, then a verdict word.

cards.head: EASY TO SWITCH
cards.text: Riders can change provider in a few minutes.

verdict.sub: Not the bikes. Not the service.

beats.notes: Let us compare what the rivals offer with what we offer, on one scale.
Rivals are cutting prices by the range shown. That is a big swing.
Our loyalty discount is much smaller, and the bracket shows the gap between the two.
Two things make it worse. Switching is easy and the rival offers are loud.
So the primary issue is price, not the bikes and not the service.

scenes.title: Three pillars keep riders.
scenes.idea: A retention plan with three supporting pillars and one promise on top.
scenes.visualDirection: Three pillars rise one by one, roof drops with a crack.

pillars.heading: PRICE
items: Loyalty discount that grows with time
Price match on rival offers for long-term riders

pillars.heading: SERVICE
items: A real person for every complaint

beats.notes: Our plan stands on three pillars.
First pillar, price. Reward loyalty and answer rival offers fairly.
Second pillar, service. Fix problems quickly and personally.
Third pillar, community. Make riding with us a shared habit.
Together they hold up one promise to every rider.

scenes.idea: Do not start a price war; build a smarter loyalty offer.
scenes.visualDirection: Strike through PRICE WAR, three moves, then a checklist ticking off.

moves.head: HOLD THE LINE
moves.text: Do not match every rival cut.

moves.head: TARGET THE LOYAL
moves.text: Reward riders who have stayed the longest.

moves.head: ASK WHY
moves.text: Talk to every rider who leaves.

checklist: Keep prices steady on the core range
Grow the loyalty discount over time

beats.notes: The tempting answer is a price war. It would hurt us more than the rivals.
The better answer is a smarter loyalty offer.
Three moves. Hold the line, target the loyal, and always ask why riders leave.
Here is the checklist we start with on Monday.

scenes.idea: Close on the idea that riders need reasons to stay.
scenes.visualDirection: Letterbox, quiet serif lines, giant final words.

inputs.line2: but good reasons to stay can bring them back.
inputs.caption: HARBOR BIKES · FICTIONAL DEMO

beats.notes: Prices may pull riders away.
But good reasons to stay can bring them back.
Give riders reasons to stay. Thank you. This was a fictional demo.
